data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise simple linking words for addition, contrast, reason, result and sequence in short A2 texts.
learningPoints: Use and and also to add information.
Use but and however to show contrast.
Use because to give a reason and so to give a result.
Use first, then and finally to show sequence.
Choose a linker that matches the relationship between ideas.
Build short connected texts rather than isolated sentences.

sections.explain: AND joins related ideas or actions.

words.word: I bought some bread and some milk.
I bought some bread because some milk.
I bought some bread but some milk.

sections.explain: ALSO adds another related fact and often comes before the main verb.

words.word: She speaks French and she also speaks Spanish.
She speaks French and also she speaks Spanish always.
She speaks French but she also speaks Spanish because.
The hotel was cheap, but it was clean.
The hotel was cheap, because it was clean.
The hotel was cheap, so but it was clean.
We stayed inside because it was raining.
We stayed inside so it was raining.
We stayed inside however it was raining.
I was hungry, so I made a sandwich.
I was hungry because I made a sandwich.
I was hungry however I made a sandwich because.

sections.summary: Using 'first' for the beginning of a sequence.
sections.explain: FIRST introduces the first step or event.

words.word: First, wash the vegetables.
Finally, wash the vegetables before the first step.
Because, wash the vegetables.
First we had lunch, then we went for a walk.
First we had lunch, because we went for a walk.
First we had lunch, however then because a walk.

sections.explain: FINALLY introduces the last event in a sequence.

words.word: Finally, we arrived at the hotel.
First, we finally arrived before we started.
Because finally, we arrived at the hotel so.

sections.explain: HOWEVER can introduce a contrasting sentence or clause, especially in writing.

words.word: The journey was long. However, it was comfortable.
The journey was long. Because, it was comfortable.
The journey was long. So however because comfortable.

sections.explain: Choose linkers according to whether the second idea is a reason or a result.

words.word: The shop was closed, so we went somewhere else.
The shop was closed, because we went somewhere else.
The shop was closed, however because we went somewhere else.
